finding.title: The `snprintf` function is used to format the HTTP request, but it does not check if the input `path` or `host` exceeds the buffer size.
The `url` and `path` are directly used in the HTTP request without any validation or sanitization.
The `port` is directly converted from a string to an integer using `atoi` without any validation.
The code does not handle errors from `fgets` properly, which can lead to incomplete or malformed input.
The code does not handle the case where `fopen` fails, which can lead to resource leaks.

findings.description: The `snprintf` function is used to format the HTTP request, but it does not check if the input `path` or `host` exceeds the buffer size.
The `url` and `path` are directly used in the HTTP request without any validation or sanitization.
The `port` is directly converted from a string to an integer using `atoi` without any validation.
The code does not handle errors from `fgets` properly, which can lead to incomplete or malformed input.
The code does not handle the case where `fopen` fails, which can lead to resource leaks.
